text_en: Move to the highest floor or the roof. Take drinking water, medicines, your phone and a torch.
If it is safe to reach, switch off the electricity mains.
Do not walk or drive through moving water. Even ankle-deep flowing water can knock you down.
Stay away from electric poles and fallen wires.
Signal rescuers from the roof with a bright cloth or a torch.
Save your phone battery: close other apps, and send an SMS if calls fail.
Drink only boiled or bottled water.
Press a clean cloth firmly on any bleeding wound.
Keep insulin dry and as cool as possible. If sugar feels low, eat something sweet.
Lay an unconscious person on their side and keep their airway clear.
Stay indoors, away from windows, until officials announce it is safe.
Move away from the slope and river channels. Listen for cracking trees or rolling stones.
Stay low under the smoke and cover your nose and mouth with a wet cloth.
If you are trapped, tap on a pipe or wall so rescuers can hear you. Do not light a match.
Your details are recorded and the control room can see you on the map.
Stay calm and stay on a high, dry place. Keep this phone with you.
